title: I pitted Cloudflare against Google DNS on Android, but speed wasn't the real surprise
content_html:
Published Aug 13, 2026, 4:00 PM EDT

Dhruv Bhutani has covered the Android ecosystem since 2010, with a focus on smartphones, connected devices, and home networking. His reporting is informed by hands-on experience reviewing hundreds of smartphones and testing a wide range of smart home and audio products over more than a decade. He has attended Mobile World Congress eight times since 2011 and IFA Berlin five times, alongside regular coverage of launch events and industry briefings from companies including Google, Xiaomi, Oppo, and Qualcomm. This on-ground access and long-term exposure to product cycles inform how he evaluates hardware, software direction, and ecosystem shifts.

Most people don't change the DNS settings on their phone for no reason. If you're looking up this option, you're usually looking for a specific utility or reason.

In my case, I didn't want every network deciding how my phone resolves websites and services. Plus, I wanted to get around certain geographical blocks.

There are a few options available to an enthusiast when it comes to swapping DNS, but Cloudflare and Google's public DNS come on top.

So, I decided to test them out head-to-head. I expected the biggest decision maker between them to be speed, but that difference is imperceptible.

Instead, what I found more interesting was that Cloudflare lets me do more than Google DNS after the fact.

Quiz

8 Questions · Test Your Knowledge

Cloudflare, Google DNS, and internet privacy on Android
Trivia challenge

Think you know your DNS resolvers and privacy settings on Android? Put your knowledge to the test.

DNSPrivacyNetworkingAndroidSecurity

01 / 8

DNS

What is the IP address of Cloudflare's primary public DNS resolver?

Correct! Cloudflare's primary DNS resolver is 1.1.1.1, launched in April 2018. It's widely praised for being one of the fastest and most privacy-focused public DNS services available.

Not quite — the answer is 1.1.1.1. That's Cloudflare's primary resolver, launched on April 1, 2018 (no joke!). 8.8.8.8 belongs to Google, while 9.9.9.9 is Quad9 and 208.67.222.222 is OpenDNS.

02 / 8

DNS

What is the IP address of Google's primary public DNS resolver?

Correct! Google's primary DNS resolver is 8.8.8.8, with 8.8.4.4 as its secondary. Google Public DNS launched in 2009 and remains one of the most widely used DNS services in the world.

Not quite — the answer is 8.8.8.8. Google Public DNS has used this memorable address since its launch in 2009. Its secondary resolver is 8.8.4.4. The 1.1.1.1 address belongs to Cloudflare.

03 / 8

Android

Which Android version first introduced native support for Private DNS, allowing users to set a custom DNS-over-TLS provider system-wide?

Correct! Android 9 Pie introduced the Private DNS feature in 2018, letting users specify a DNS-over-TLS provider across all network connections. This was a major step forward for mobile privacy.

Not quite — it was Android 9 Pie. Google added the Private DNS setting in 2018, enabling DNS-over-TLS system-wide without needing a VPN or third-party app. You can still find it today under Settings > Network & internet > Private DNS.

04 / 8

Privacy

What does DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) primarily protect against compared to traditional DNS?

Correct! DNS-over-HTTPS encrypts your DNS queries inside HTTPS traffic, preventing ISPs, network operators, or attackers from seeing or tampering with which domains you're looking up. It's a key privacy enhancement over plain DNS.

Not quite — the primary protection DoH offers is against eavesdropping and tampering with your DNS queries. Traditional DNS sends lookups in plain text, meaning anyone on the network path can see or alter them. DoH wraps those queries in encrypted HTTPS to prevent this.

05 / 8

Android

On a modern Android device, where would you navigate to set a system-wide Private DNS provider like 1.1.1.1?

Correct! On stock Android, Private DNS lives under Settings > Network & internet > Private DNS. You can enter a hostname like 1dot1dot1dot1.cloudflare-dns.com to use Cloudflare's DNS-over-TLS resolver system-wide.

Not quite — on stock Android, the Private DNS option is found under Settings > Network & internet > Private DNS. Note that Samsung's One UI rearranges some menus, but the standard Android path is consistent across Pixel and many other devices.

06 / 8

Networking

Cloudflare offers a privacy-focused DNS variant at 1.1.1.2 that blocks access to what type of content?

Correct! Cloudflare's 1.1.1.2 resolver is designed to block known malware and phishing domains, adding a layer of protection without needing extra software. Cloudflare also offers 1.1.1.3, which additionally blocks adult content.

Not quite — 1.1.1.2 blocks malware and phishing sites. Cloudflare offers a tiered set of resolvers: 1.1.1.1 for speed and privacy, 1.1.1.2 for malware blocking, and 1.1.1.3 for both malware and adult content filtering.

07 / 8

Security

What is the hostname used to configure Cloudflare's DNS-over-TLS resolver in Android's Private DNS setting?

Correct! Because Android's Private DNS field requires a hostname rather than an IP address, Cloudflare provides 1dot1dot1dot1.cloudflare-dns.com as the DNS-over-TLS hostname. It's a clever workaround for a field that doesn't accept raw IPs.

Not quite — the correct hostname is 1dot1dot1dot1.cloudflare-dns.com. Android's Private DNS field needs a resolvable hostname, not a raw IP like 1.1.1.1, so Cloudflare created this hostname specifically for use in that setting.

08 / 8

DNS

Which protocol does Android's built-in Private DNS feature use to encrypt DNS traffic?

Correct! Android's Private DNS feature uses DNS-over-TLS (DoT), which operates on port 853 and wraps DNS queries in a TLS-encrypted connection. This is different from DNS-over-HTTPS, which tunnels DNS inside regular HTTPS traffic on port 443.

Not quite — Android's Private DNS uses DNS-over-TLS (DoT), not DNS-over-HTTPS. DoT runs on its own dedicated port (853), making it easy for network administrators to identify and potentially block, whereas DoH blends into regular web traffic on port 443.

Private DNS gives me a consistent resolver across all networks

DNS encryption adds protection without the overhead of running a VPN

When it comes to swapping out the DNS, Android's Private DNS feature is the starting point for everyone.

You can enter a provider hostname and have the phone use DNS over TLS instead of using the resolver provided by your network provider.

This could be your wireless carrier or even your home broadband when you're connected over Wi-Fi. And getting started is very simple.

Both Google and Cloudflare provide a URL that you enter into your private DNS setting. In the case of Google, this is dns.google.com, while Cloudflare uses 1.1.1.1.

After you've applied the private DNS setting, it works across your Wi-Fi and cellular connections.

That last part is important because you probably switch between data providers multiple times a day.

When you leave home, you switch over to your wireless carrier, and maybe when you get to a coffee shop or office, you'll switch over to their Wi-Fi network.

Setting a private DNS means that all DNS resolution happens through the same single resolver.

So what does that mean?

Using private DNS standardizes one part of your network connectivity. For example, if a website works on one connection and not on another, you can eliminate DNS as one of the issues. This problem arises more often than you'd imagine.

Both Cloudflare and Google's DNS resolvers tend to be very fast, so you can expect slightly faster browsing all around.

Elsewhere, there's encryption. It's not a VPN, and a private DNS can only protect DNS traffic, but both Google and Cloudflare support DNS over DLS and over HTTPS.

A portion of your traffic remains fully encrypted, and that portion is the one that sends out queries to the internet. You don't really need a VPN for everyday browsing, but that's only the start.

Cloudflare gives you more flexibility than Google DNS

Google DNS is the set it and forget it option

Testing both DNS resolvers, I quickly realized that speed is just the start.

While both DNS resolvers are equally fast for all practical purposes, Google's public DNS is a great set-it-and-forget-it option, but not the one to pick if you want a bit more flexibility.

That's where Cloudflare steps up. While Cloudflare's default 1.1.1.1 resolver gives you standard DNS resolution without additional content filtering, you have options.

For example, Cloudflare offers a specific resolver designed for family use. One of these DNS resolvers can block domains associated with malware and phishing, making it a great choice for households that might not be up to speed with the best internet safety practices.

Elsewhere, it offers a DNS resolver that can block adult content across your network. This is an excellent choice for households with young children, and it automatically blocks any unapproved content on all devices, including smartphones, tablets, and laptops.

All it takes is changing one setting at the phone or router level, and it handles everything else.

Using Cloudflare as your DNS resolver also gives you access to WARP. If you use Cloudflare's app, it lets you switch between DNS-only mode and Warp mode.

In DNS-only mode, it works like Private DNS, where it encrypts your DNS queries. That's it. WARP goes further by tunneling your devices' entire traffic through Cloudflare's network.

This gives you all the security and encryption benefits of using a VPN. Keeping in mind that this is not a traditional VPN, you cannot change your geolocation on the fly using WARP.

The idea here is that if you want to secure your entire traffic over a network that you don't entirely trust, let's say public Wi-Fi, that's where WARP comes in.

When comparing Google DNS and Cloudflare's Private DNS, this flexibility stands out. The numbers are more than fast enough that you won't notice a difference.

However, Cloudflare gives you the option to filter content and encrypt the entirety of your traffic. That's something that Google DNS doesn't offer, but on the flip side, Google DNS gives you a little more simplicity.

Cloudflare wins out for being more than a simple DNS resolver

The choice between them depends on your goal.

If you want the simplest way to get around your network provider's DNS restrictions, Google DNS is probably the way to go.

If you're like me, and you like the ability to tweak your experience and definitely don't mind a free VPN-like service as an add-on, I would recommend going the Cloudflare route. It gives you all the speed with a side of security. Can't complain about that.

blocks.html_en: What does DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) primarily protect against compared to traditional DNS?

sentences.en: What does DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) primarily protect against compared to traditional DNS?
sentences.zh: 与传统 DNS 相比，DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) 主要防范什么？

sentences.en: AMalware infections from malicious websitesBEavesdropping and tampering of DNS queries by third partiesCIP address spoofing attacks on routersDSlower DNS resolution speeds on mobile networks
sentences.zh: A来自恶意网站的恶意软件感染B第三方窃听和篡改 DNS 查询对路由器的 CIP 地址欺骗攻击D移动网络上的 DNS 解析速度较低

blocks.html_en: Correct! DNS-over-HTTPS encrypts your DNS queries inside HTTPS traffic, preventing ISPs, network operators, or attackers from seeing or tampering with which domains you're looking up. It's a key privacy enhancement over plain DNS.

sentences.en: Correct!
sentences.zh: 正确的！

sentences.en: DNS-over-HTTPS encrypts your DNS queries inside HTTPS traffic, preventing ISPs, network operators, or attackers from seeing or tampering with which domains you're looking up.
sentences.zh: DNS-over-HTTPS 对 HTTPS 流量内的 DNS 查询进行加密，防止 ISP、网络运营商或攻击者查看或篡改您正在查找的域。

sentences.en: It's a key privacy enhancement over plain DNS.
sentences.zh: 与普通 DNS 相比，这是一项关键的隐私增强功能。

blocks.html_en: Not quite — the primary protection DoH offers is against eavesdropping and tampering with your DNS queries. Traditional DNS sends lookups in plain text, meaning anyone on the network path can see or alter them. DoH wraps those queries in encrypted HTTPS to prevent this.

sentences.en: Not quite — the primary protection DoH offers is against eavesdropping and tampering with your DNS queries.
sentences.zh: 不完全是——DoH 提供的主要保护是防止窃听和篡改您的 DNS 查询。

sentences.en: Traditional DNS sends lookups in plain text, meaning anyone on the network path can see or alter them.
sentences.zh: 传统 DNS 以纯文本形式发送查找，这意味着网络路径上的任何人都可以查看或更改它们。

sentences.en: DoH wraps those queries in encrypted HTTPS to prevent this.
sentences.zh: DoH 将这些查询包装在加密的 HTTPS 中以防止这种情况发生。

Which protocol does Android's built-in Private DNS feature use to encrypt DNS traffic?

sentences.en: Which protocol does Android's built-in Private DNS feature use to encrypt DNS traffic?
sentences.zh: Android 的内置私有 DNS 功能使用哪种协议来加密 DNS 流量？

sentences.en: ADNS-over-HTTPS (DoH)BDNS-over-QUIC (DoQ)CDNS-over-TLS (DoT)DDNSCrypt

blocks.html_en: Correct! Android's Private DNS feature uses DNS-over-TLS (DoT), which operates on port 853 and wraps DNS queries in a TLS-encrypted connection. This is different from DNS-over-HTTPS, which tunnels DNS inside regular HTTPS traffic on port 443.

sentences.en: Correct!
sentences.zh: 正确的！

sentences.en: Android's Private DNS feature uses DNS-over-TLS (DoT), which operates on port 853 and wraps DNS queries in a TLS-encrypted connection.
sentences.zh: Android 的私有 DNS 功能使用 DNS-over-TLS (DoT)，它在端口 853 上运行，并将 DNS 查询包装在 TLS 加密连接中。

sentences.en: This is different from DNS-over-HTTPS, which tunnels DNS inside regular HTTPS traffic on port 443.
sentences.zh: 这与 DNS-over-HTTPS 不同，后者在端口 443 上的常规 HTTPS 流量内传输 DNS。

blocks.html_en: Not quite — Android's Private DNS uses DNS-over-TLS (DoT), not DNS-over-HTTPS. DoT runs on its own dedicated port (853), making it easy for network administrators to identify and potentially block, whereas DoH blends into regular web traffic on port 443.

sentences.en: Not quite — Android's Private DNS uses DNS-over-TLS (DoT), not DNS-over-HTTPS.

sentences.en: DoT runs on its own dedicated port (853), making it easy for network administrators to identify and potentially block, whereas DoH blends into regular web traffic on port 443.
sentences.zh: DoT 在其自己的专用端口 (853) 上运行，使网络管理员可以轻松识别并可能进行阻止，而 DoH 则在端口 443 上混合到常规 Web 流量中。

大多数人不会无缘无故地更改手机上的 DNS 设置。 如果您正在查找此选项，您通常是在寻找特定的实用程序或原因。

就我而言，我不希望每个网络都决定我的手机如何解析网站和服务。 另外，我想绕过某些地理区域。

在交换 DNS 方面，爱好者可以选择一些选项，但 Cloudflare 和 Google 的公共 DNS 是最重要的。

因此，我决定对它们进行面对面的测试。 我预计它们之间最大的决策者是速度，但这种差异是难以察觉的。

相反，我发现更有趣的是，事后 Cloudflare 让我可以做比 Google DNS 更多的事情。

Cloudflare 的主要公共 DNS 解析器的 IP 地址是什么？

正确的！ Cloudflare 的主要 DNS 解析器是 1.1.1.1，于 2018 年 4 月推出。 它被广泛赞誉为最快、最注重隐私的公共 DNS 服务之一。

不完全是——答案是 1.1.1.1。 这是 Cloudflare 的主要解析器，于 2018 年 4 月 1 日推出（不是开玩笑！）。 8.8.8.8 属于 Google，9.9.9.9 属于 Quad9，208.67.222.222 属于 OpenDNS。

Google 主要公共 DNS 解析器的 IP 地址是什么？

正确的！ Google 的主要 DNS 解析器是 8.8.8.8，次要解析器是 8.8.4.4。 Google 公共 DNS 于 2009 年推出，至今仍然是世界上使用最广泛的 DNS 服务之一。

不完全是——答案是 8.8.8.8。 谷歌公共 DNS 自 2009 年推出以来一直使用这个令人难忘的地址。 其辅助解析器是 8.8.4.4。 1.1.1.1 地址属于 Cloudflare。

哪个 Android 版本首先引入了对私有 DNS 的本机支持，允许用户在系统范围内设置自定义 DNS-over-TLS 提供商？

AAndroid 7.0 NougatBAndroid 8.0 OreoCAndroid 9 PieDAndroid 10

正确的！ Android 9 Pie 于 2018 年引入了私有 DNS 功能，允许用户在所有网络连接上指定 DNS-over-TLS 提供商。 这是移动隐私方面向前迈出的重要一步。

不完全是——它是 Android 9 Pie。 Google 在 2018 年添加了私有 DNS 设置，无需 VPN 或第三方应用程序即可在系统范围内启用 DNS-over-TLS。 今天您仍然可以在“设置”>“网络和互联网”>“私有 DNS”下找到它。

与传统 DNS 相比，DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) 主要防范什么？

A来自恶意网站的恶意软件感染B第三方窃听和篡改 DNS 查询对路由器的 CIP 地址欺骗攻击D移动网络上的 DNS 解析速度较低

正确的！ DNS-over-HTTPS 对 HTTPS 流量内的 DNS 查询进行加密，防止 ISP、网络运营商或攻击者查看或篡改您正在查找的域。 与普通 DNS 相比，这是一项关键的隐私增强功能。

不完全是——DoH 提供的主要保护是防止窃听和篡改您的 DNS 查询。 传统 DNS 以纯文本形式发送查找，这意味着网络路径上的任何人都可以查看或更改它们。 DoH 将这些查询包装在加密的 HTTPS 中以防止这种情况发生。

Adns.cloudflare.comBcloudflare-dns.comC1dot1dot1dot1.cloudflare-dns.comDsecure.1.1.1.1.cloudflare.net

正确的！ 由于 Android 的私有 DNS 字段需要主机名而不是 IP 地址，因此 Cloudflare 提供 1dot1dot1dot1.cloudflare-dns.com 作为 DNS-over-TLS 主机名。 对于不接受原始 IP 的领域来说，这是一个聪明的解决方法。

不完全是——正确的主机名是 1dot1dot1dot1.cloudflare-dns.com。 Android 的私有 DNS 字段需要可解析的主机名，而不是像 1.1.1.1 这样的原始 IP，因此 Cloudflare 创建了专门用于该设置的主机名。

ADNS-over-HTTPS (DoH)BDNS-over-QUIC (DoQ)CDNS-over-TLS (DoT)DDNSCrypt

正确的！ Android 的私有 DNS 功能使用 DNS-over-TLS (DoT)，它在端口 853 上运行，并将 DNS 查询包装在 TLS 加密连接中。 这与 DNS-over-HTTPS 不同，后者在端口 443 上的常规 HTTPS 流量内传输 DNS。

私有 DNS 为我提供了跨所有网络的一致解析器

DNS 加密增强了保护，无需运行 VPN 的开销

当谈到更换 DNS 时，Android 的私有 DNS 功能是每个人的起点。

您可以输入提供商主机名，并让电话使用基于 TLS 的 DNS，而不是使用网络提供商提供的解析程序。

当您通过 Wi-Fi 连接时，这可能是您的无线运营商，甚至是您的家庭宽带。 入门非常简单。

Google 和 Cloudflare 都提供了一个 URL，您可以将其输入到您的私有 DNS 设置中。 对于 Google，这是 dns.google.com，而 Cloudflare 使用 1.1.1.1。

应用专用 DNS 设置后，它就可以在您的 Wi-Fi 和蜂窝网络连接中发挥作用。

最后一部分很重要，因为您可能每天在数据提供者之间切换多次。

当您离开家时，您会切换到无线运营商，也许当您到达咖啡店或办公室时，您会切换到他们的 Wi-Fi 网络。

设置私有 DNS 意味着所有 DNS 解析都通过同一个解析器进行。

那么这是什么意思呢？

使用私有 DNS 可以标准化网络连接的一部分。 例如，如果网站在一个连接上运行，而在另一个连接上运行失败，则您可以消除 DNS 这一问题。 这个问题出现的频率比您想象的要高。

Cloudflare 和 Google 的 DNS 解析器都非常快，因此您可以预期浏览速度会稍快一些。

在其他地方，还有加密。 它不是 VPN，私有 DNS 只能保护 DNS 流量，但 Google 和 Cloudflare 都支持基于 DLS 和 HTTPS 的 DNS。

您的一部分流量保持完全加密，并且该部分是向互联网发送查询的流量。 您实际上并不需要 VPN 来进行日常浏览，但这只是开始。

Cloudflare 为您提供比 Google DNS 更大的灵活性

Google DNS 是“一劳永逸”选项

测试了两个 DNS 解析器后，我很快意识到速度只是一个开始。

虽然这两种 DNS 解析器在所有实际用途上都同样快速，但 Google 的公共 DNS 是一个很好的“一劳永逸”选项，但如果您想要更大的灵活性，则不适合选择。

这就是 Cloudflare 发挥作用的地方。 虽然 Cloudflare 的默认 1.1.1.1 解析器为您提供标准 DNS 解析，无需额外的内容过滤，但您还有其他选择。

例如，Cloudflare 提供了专为家庭使用而设计的特定解析器。 这些 DNS 解析器之一可以阻止与恶意软件和网络钓鱼相关的域，这对于可能无法跟上最佳互联网安全实践的家庭来说是一个不错的选择。

在其他地方，它提供了一个 DNS 解析器，可以阻止网络上的成人内容。 对于有小孩的家庭来说，这是一个绝佳的选择，它会自动阻止所有设备（包括智能手机、平板电脑和笔记本电脑）上的任何未经批准的内容。

只需更改手机或路由器级别的一项设置，它就可以处理其他所有事情。

使用 Cloudflare 作为 DNS 解析器还可以让您访问 WARP。 如果您使用 Cloudflare 的应用程序，它可以让您在仅 DNS 模式和 Warp 模式之间切换。

在仅 DNS 模式下，它的工作方式类似于私有 DNS，它会加密您的 DNS 查询。 就是这样。 WARP 更进一步，通过 Cloudflare 网络传输您设备的全部流量。

这为您提供了使用 VPN 的所有安全和加密优势。 请记住，这不是传统的 VPN，您无法使用 WARP 动态更改您的地理位置。

这里的想法是，如果您想保护您不完全信任的网络（例如公共 Wi-Fi）上的全部流量，那么 WARP 就可以发挥作用。

在比较 Google DNS 和 Cloudflare 的私有 DNS 时，这种灵活性非常突出。 这些数字足够快，您不会注意到差异。

但是，Cloudflare 为您提供了过滤内容和加密整个流量的选项。 这是 Google DNS 不提供的功能，但另一方面，Google DNS 为您提供了更多的简单性。

Cloudflare 因其不仅仅是一个简单的 DNS 解析器而胜出

它们之间的选择取决于您的目标。

如果您想要以最简单的方式绕过网络提供商的 DNS 限制，Google DNS 可能是您的最佳选择。

如果您像我一样，并且喜欢调整体验的能力，并且绝对不介意将类似 VPN 的免费服务作为附加组件，那么我建议您选择 Cloudflare 路线。 它为您提供了所有的速度和安全性。 不能对此抱怨。
